findings.summary: A rules_considered id counts as resolved on the KERNEL- prefix alone, so a value-shaped id such as KERNEL-buyer@example.com or KERNEL-84901234567 (allowed by RefId) is stored verbatim in proposal.created rationale/step_rationales, and from there in the evidence bundle and explain. The prefix does not resolve it to anything real, which is the gap P-1 was meant to close (PR-26, ADR 0033 §4). Reproduced: check_rationale([r], set(), set(), {'run'}) gives resolved=True, and at_rest stores rules_considered=['KERNEL-buyer@example.com']. Fix only the at-rest split: store a KERNEL-* id verbatim only when it is one of the kernel's real finding ids, else as its digest. Leave check_rationale's startswith resolution unchanged, because the brief forbids a new repair finding.

No test puts a value-shaped or unresolved ref in a plan's step rationale and checks that step_rationales in proposal.created (plan_flow.py:278 via RationaleProbe.stored) holds only digests. The digest-only sink tests cover just the single-proposal path and typed or grounded answer citations, so the plan sink depends on code being shared, not on a test.

ADR 0033 §4 and the target architecture still describe goal_ref as task definition id@version plus acceptance item, recorded and shown, and the old verbatim at-rest form. The contract docstrings now state the narrowed closed set and the digest keys, so design and code disagree. Both paths were outside this task's scope, so this needs a follow-up edit or ADR note (AGENTS.md: update designs when contracts change).
